subtitle: A new recruit claims a place in Stilwater

body: Saints Row is Volition's Xbox 360 open-world action game, first released in North America on 29 August 2006. A player-created character joins the 3rd Street Saints after the gang saves their life, then helps it challenge rival organisations across Stilwater. The city can be explored on foot or by vehicle, with story missions and smaller activities drawing the player into its districts. The campaign is divided between opposing gangs rather than one uninterrupted chain of assignments. Building a reputation becomes the means of deciding which part of that struggle to pursue next.

Activities and side missions award Respect, which is spent to unlock story missions. The system makes the city's diversions part of the campaign's progress rather than leaving them entirely outside it. Driving, shooting and calling on gang allies provide familiar tools for dealing with the work that follows. Customising the protagonist helps make the rise through the Saints feel like the player's own career. Stilwater becomes useful through repeated visits, as a district contains both the next conflict and an activity that can supply the standing needed to begin it.

Steve Jaros wrote the story for a project published by THQ. Reviews were positive, often comparing its open-world design favourably with Grand Theft Auto, and sales passed one million copies by the end of 2006. Online multiplayer added cooperative and competitive activities beyond the single-player city. Its success led to Saints Row 2 in 2008 and a franchise that would become increasingly extravagant. The original remains a more grounded introduction to the Saints, establishing the created protagonist, rival gangs and expandable city that gave the later games their starting point.
